title: The selected finite-stage datum satisfies the gluing axioms
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with its selected finite affine gluing presentation $\mathsf G_S$ [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation]. Use the raw coefficient tuple $C$ at $c=\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ of [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage] and the explicit raw refinement system $I(C)$ of [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]: its chart rings $B_{a,i}\subseteq A_a=\Gamma(U_a,\mathcal O_S)$ are finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subrings containing $C_a$ and the labelled principal-open elements $f_p$, and each labelled original restriction $\rho_p:A_b\to(A_a)_{f_p}$ restricts to $\rho_{p,i}:B_{b,i}\to(B_{a,i})_{f_p}$. Transitions are inclusions and their explicit fraction maps, not unspecified extensions between independent rings. Write $X_{a,i}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{a,i}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $P_{p,i}=D_{B_{a,i}}(f_p)$ for its labelled source pieces, and $W_{ab,i}$ for the union of the pieces $p:a\to b$. Localizations are as in [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. No gluing equations are assumed of a raw tuple.

Use exactly the selected finite open and localized map witnesses, upper-bound parameters and index $j=\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$ of [def-nagata-affine-gluing-valid-stage] on this same system $I(C)$. Then the labelled piece maps in its raw datum at $j$ agree on intersections and assemble into morphisms $\varphi_{ab,j}:W_{ab,j}\to W_{ba,j}$. These preserve the selected opens, are mutually inverse, and satisfy all identity and triple-overlap cocycle equations. Explicitly,
$$W_{aa,j}=X_{a,j},\qquad\varphi_{aa,j}=\mathrm{id},\qquad\varphi_{ba,j}\circ\varphi_{ab,j}=\mathrm{id}_{W_{ab,j}},$$
and for every triple $(a,b,d)$,
$$\varphi_{ab,j}^{-1}(W_{ba,j}\cap W_{bd,j})=W_{ab,j}\cap W_{ad,j},\qquad\varphi_{bd,j}\circ\varphi_{ab,j}=\varphi_{ad,j}\ \text{on }W_{ab,j}\cap W_{ad,j}.$$

proof.text: Use the same coefficient system and choices as [def-nagata-affine-gluing-valid-stage], rather than constructing another notion of refinement. The initial tuple $C$ comes from [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage]; [lemma-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficients-descend] identifies its restricted maps with the original restrictions. The definition [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system] specifies every tuple, labelled principal piece, inclusion, localized comparison and actual composite domain. The statement [lem-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-cofinal] supplies nonemptiness, directedness and chartwise cofinality for this very system. In particular the upper-bound choices fixed in the valid-stage definition are defined on $I(C)$. Keep its test list $E$: diagonal cover, piecewise image-in-overlap and triple-domain open tests in both orientations, agreement on piece intersections, diagonal identity, both inverse comparisons, and every labelled triple comparison. None of these gluing equations is part of the definition of a raw tuple. This reuses the existing system; no downstream valid-refinement or glued-scheme theorem is used.

source.place: ## Proof; independent second reading using the current explicit raw-refinement and witness interfaces; step 1

proof.text: Let $F_S=\{c\}\cup\{w_e:e\in E\}$ be the finite set in [def-nagata-affine-gluing-valid-stage]. By [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound], each $w_e$ and $c$ is at most $j=u(F_S)$, with exactly that definition's fixed upper-bound parameters. All transitions are the inclusions and fraction maps of [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]. For ANY $v\in B_{a,j}$ the induced map $e_{a,j,v}:(B_{a,j})_v\to(A_a)_v$ is injective: equality of the images of $x/v^r$ and $y/v^s$ means $v^k(v^sx-v^ry)=0$ in $A_a$ for some $k$, by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. This same equation holds in its subring $B_{a,j}$, proving the fraction equality there. This includes nilpotent $v$, products of principal-open elements, and new numerator elements. Thus for every labelled piece $p:a\to b$ and EVERY final $z\in B_{b,j}$, the restricted map is uniquely characterized by $e_{a,j,f_p}(\rho_{p,j}(z))=\rho_p(z)$. Its existence is the defining image-containment condition of a tuple. Both sides of the piece-map comparison square have this same image, so they commute on all final elements. No old generator list is being treated as a generating set for an enlarged ring.

source.place: ## Proof; independent second reading using the current explicit raw-refinement and witness interfaces; step 2

proof.text:
Verify the open tests piecewise, before assuming local maps glue. A basic open defined by an old element is the inverse image of that basic open under a chart inclusion: a prime avoids the element if and only if its contraction avoids it. On each labelled piece $p:a\to b$, the commuting comparison of [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system] therefore gives, for any open $V_w\subseteq X_{b,w}$,
$$p_j^{-1}((q^b_{jw})^{-1}V_w)=(q^p_{jw})^{-1}(p_w^{-1}V_w),$$
where $q^p$ is the piece comparison. By [def-nagata-affine-gluing-valid-stage], the open witnesses are explicit positive-power identities $h_i^{N_i}=\sum_k a_{ik}g_k$ and $g_k^{M_k}=\sum_i b_{ki}h_i$ on localized principal domains, with their numerator coefficients and annihilating powers retained at $w_e$. Applying its transition to $j$ preserves these ring equalities. If a prime contains all $g_k$, it contains every $h_i^{N_i}$ and hence every $h_i$; the reverse identities give the converse. Taking complements proves equality of the two finite unions of basic opens at $j$, including on each actual inverse-image/intersection domain. Thus the diagonal test gives $W_{aa,j}=X_{a,j}$, each image test gives $p_j^{-1}(W_{ba,j})=P_{p,j}$, and each domain test gives $p_j^{-1}(W_{bd,j})=P_{p,j}\cap W_{ad,j}$. The same tests are present for reversed pieces. The prime and inverse-image calculations use [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; they do not use surjectivity or a Cartesian square between different charts.

source.place: ## Proof; independent second reading using the current explicit raw-refinement and witness interfaces; step 3

proof.text:
Verify every map test on all final coefficients by faithful localization. If $p:a\to b$ is represented on $D(f_p)$ and the next piece is $D_{B_b}(t)$, write $\rho_{p,j}(t)=h/f_p^N$. Its actual inverse-image domain is $D(f_ph)$, and the extension on fractions is explicitly
$$y/t^k\longmapsto\rho_{p,j}(y)f_p^{Nk}/h^k.$$
This follows directly from [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and agrees with the original localized restriction after inclusion into $(A_a)_{f_ph}$. Iterating this formula and multiplying the source and numerator elements puts every parallel comparison on principal pieces $D(v)$ with both ring maps landing in the SAME $(B_{a,j})_v$, as specified by [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]. For two such maps $P_j,Q_j:B_{d,j}\to(B_{a,j})_v$, their original counterparts $P,Q:A_d\to(A_a)_v$ satisfy, for each final $z\in B_{d,j}$,
$$e_{a,j,v}(P_j(z))=P(z)=Q(z)=e_{a,j,v}(Q_j(z)).$$
Here the middle equality is an explicitly recorded equality of the original presentation [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation]. For agreement of two pieces into chart $b$, take their two restriction maps on $D(f_pf_{p'})$; both originals are the same overlap identification restricted to that intersection. For a diagonal comparison take $P_j$ to be the restricted identity and $Q_j=\rho_{p,j}$ for a diagonal piece. For an inverse on chart $a$, take $P_j$ to be the chart inclusion's ring map and $Q_j=\rho_{p,j}^{\mathrm{loc}}\circ\rho_{q,j}$, with $p:a\to b$ and $q:b\to a$; the opposite inverse uses the ordered pair $(b,a)$. For a triple take $P_j=\rho_{r,j}$ and $Q_j=\rho_{p,j}^{\mathrm{loc}}\circ\rho_{q,j}$, where $p:a\to b$, $q:b\to d$, and $r:a\to d$, restricting to the common domain of these labelled pieces. The superscript denotes the displayed fraction extension. These are all map tests of [def-nagata-affine-gluing-valid-stage], including every piece combination. In each case step 2 gives $P_j(z)=Q_j(z)$ for every final $z$, and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives equality of the corresponding affine-source scheme maps. Thus the enlarged target's new generators satisfy the tests too, without inferring this from tests on the generators at $c$.

source.place: ## Proof; independent second reading using the current explicit raw-refinement and witness interfaces; step 4

proof.text:
For each pair $(a,b)$, its finitely many principal pieces cover $W_{ab,j}$ by [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]. Step 4 proves their maps into $X_{b,j}$ agree on every intersection, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] assembles them into a unique $g_{ab,j}:W_{ab,j}\to X_{b,j}$. Step 3 puts the image of each piece in $W_{ba,j}$; restrict the point and structure-sheaf maps to that open to obtain $\varphi_{ab,j}:W_{ab,j}\to W_{ba,j}$. On each piece, step 3's domain equation gives the inverse image of $W_{bd,j}$ as $P_{p,j}\cap W_{ad,j}$; union over its covering proves exactly
$$\varphi_{ab,j}^{-1}(W_{ba,j}\cap W_{bd,j})=W_{ab,j}\cap W_{ad,j}.$$
For the diagonal, $W_{aa,j}=X_{a,j}$ and each diagonal piece map equals its chart inclusion by step 4; uniqueness in the same gluing lemma gives $\varphi_{aa,j}=\mathrm{id}$. For the inverse, cover $W_{ab,j}$ by the first pieces and their inverse images of the reverse pieces, which cover it by step 3. The two composites there equal the corresponding inclusions by step 4, so gluing uniqueness gives $\varphi_{ba,j}\varphi_{ab,j}=\mathrm{id}$; apply this separately with $(b,a)$ to obtain the reverse identity. For the triple, the domain equation just proved identifies the composite domain with $W_{ab,j}\cap W_{ad,j}$. Intersect a first piece, the inverse image of a second piece, and a direct piece to cover that domain. Every such labelled comparison is equal by step 4, hence gluing uniqueness gives $\varphi_{bd,j}\varphi_{ab,j}=\varphi_{ad,j}$ there. Equalities into the ambient target chart are also equalities into the specified open target because their point and sheaf maps restrict identically. These are precisely all equations listed in [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation].
